results.title: Sodium - New World Encyclopedia
results.snippet: Sodium (chemical symbol Na, atomic number 11) is a member of a group of chemical elements known as alkali metals. Silvery in color, it is soft, waxy, and lightweight.

results.title: Sodium - Wikipedia
results.snippet: Symbol. "Na": from New Latin natrium, coined from German Natron, 'natron'. Isotopes of sodium.Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium. ) and atomic number 11. It is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal.

results.snippet: Name:Sodium. Symbol:Na. Type:Alkali Metal.The chemical symbol for sodium (Na) comes from the Latin word 'natrium' meaning hydrated sodium carbonate.

results.title: Sodium (Na) - The Chemical Elements
results.snippet: Sodium is a chemical element with atomic number 11 in the periodic table. It's the fourth most abundant element and comprises around 2.6% of Earth’s crust.

results.title: Chemical Symbol for Sodium - Na
results.snippet: The chemical symbol for Sodium is Na. Sodium is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal. Sodium is an alkali metal, being in group 1 of the periodic table, because it has a single electron in its outer shell that it readily donates, creating a positively charged atom—the Na+ cation.

results.title: Sodium Facts, Symbol, Discovery, Properties, Uses
results.snippet: The Latin word for sodium carbonate, “natrium” is the origin of its chemical symbol [1, 2].
